items.title: Vercel Security Review now in public beta
items.summary: is now in public beta for Pro and Enterprise teams. Once enabled, every push to a connected GitHub repository is automatically reviewed for vulnerabilities, and findings are reported in the .Vercel Security ReviewVulnerabilities dashboardSecurity Review runs automatically when code is pushed to a connected GitHub repository. Because reviews start from push events rather than pull requests, direct and force pushes to your production branch are reviewed as well. Every project affected by a single push is reviewed together.Each finding records the project, environment, branch, and commit, with a summary, a suggested fix, and an AI-generated severity rating.Security Review adds its own GitHub check to each commit it reviews. When there's a pull request, it also posts findings as review comments that link back to each finding. On public repositories, finding details stay in the dashboard.Clicking  on a vulnerability report hands the finding to Vercel Agent, which proposes a fix and opens a pull request for you to review. Nothing merges until you approve it.Fix with Vercel AgentTo fix findings with your coding agent instead, use  in the Vercel CLI, or copy any finding as Markdown or JSON.vercel security vulnerabilitiesTeams can write security policies in plain language, for all projects or specific ones, to give Security Review more context about how they build. Set a team policy in Agent settings and a project policy in the project's Security settings.Security Review analyzes source code. It isn't a security audit, and it doesn't perform runtime or penetration testing. It helps you find vulnerabilities but doesn't guarantee your application is free of them.Security Review is billed at the : provider inference at the underlying token rate with no markup, plus the Vercel Token Rate of $0.25 per million tokens (input, cached, output). Reviews run on each push to GitHub, so cost scales with how often you push and how much code changes.Vercel Agent rateSecurity reviews are free until November 10, 2026, and fixes made with Vercel Agent are billed at the Vercel Agent rate.Enable Security Review in your , or read the  and the  to learn more. The CLI command needs Vercel CLI 65.10.0 or later.team’s Agent settingsdocumentationannouncementRead moreWhat triggers a reviewWhat a finding includesFixes and resolutionSecurity policiesLimitationsPricing

items.title: Diagnose Vercel CLI setup problems with vercel doctor
items.summary: Vercel CLI now includes , which checks your setup and shows the command that fixes each problem it finds.vercel doctorIt checks the CLI version and install, your login and current team, the project link, and your project configuration in . It also reports active incidents from the Vercel status page.vercel.jsonEach check reports OK, Warning, Failed, or Skipped. When vercel upgrade can't update the installed CLI, the install check shows where the CLI runs from and how to reinstall it.Doctor runs without a login or a linked project, and it never prompts, logs in, or links a project, so coding agents can run it before guessing at a fix. Add --json to get each check's status and suggested commands as structured output.Update to the latest CLI version and run  to check your setup, or read the doctor command reference.vercel doctorRead more

items.title: Introducing Vercel Security Review
items.summary: Today, we are launching  in public beta.Vercel Security ReviewSecurity Review is a new capability in , alongside Code Review and Investigation. Once enabled, it scans for vulnerabilities on every push to a team's connected GitHub repositories.Vercel AgentFindings appear as comments on pull requests, are listed in the Security dashboard, and are available via CLI. With your permission, Vercel Agent can also validate and push fixes for findings.Security reviews are triggered by GitHub push events, including direct pushes to your production branch. In monorepos, reviews are scoped to the project's root directory. Here is how it works: Each review compares the push against a base and covers only what changed. For deployments, the base is the branch’s previous deployment, so the agent reviews the change against what’s already running. Because it only scans the diff, Security Review finishes in seconds and can run on every preview and production deployment.The agent reads the diff along with the surrounding code, traces how the changed code can be reached, checks for existing protections, and rechecks each finding before reporting it. That process is how it catches logic flaws like missing authorization checks, which pattern-matching scanners miss.Each review also applies your team’s , which you can write in plain language and apply to specific projects or across your team. For example, a policy can require any endpoint that returns customer data to check that the requester owns it. You can also manage policies with the Vercel CLI, using .security policiesvercel security policyEach new finding is checked against ones that have already been reported, so the same issue isn’t flagged twice. Every finding is tied to the deployment where it first appeared and changes are followed from there. That means that when a vulnerable change from a pull request is merged into your production branch, the finding is flagged in production as well.When a later review no longer detects the issue in an environment, the agent marks the finding as no longer detected there.Every finding explains the vulnerability and how to fix it, with links to the commit and deployment where it first appeared. Findings are listed in the  in the Security dashboard, where you can ask Vercel Agent to validate and commit fixes. Findings are also , so you can fix vulnerabilities with your own coding agent. Vulnerability viewavailable via CLIEach new finding generates an audit log event, which Enterprise teams can send to their SIEM through .Audit Log DrainsHere is a demo of sample findings in the dashboard:When Vercel Agent can fix a finding, you will see the option to click  on the finding page in the dashboard. After you click, the agent confirms the vulnerability still exists, then makes the smallest change that fixes it and updates the tests.Fix with Vercel AgentSay a developer pushes a change to an invoice download endpoint, and the lookup doesn't check which organization the invoice belongs to. Within seconds, Security Review flags that any signed-in user could download another organization's invoice by changing its ID. Vercel Agent's fix scopes the lookup to the user's organization:You can point your coding agent or other systems at the Vercel CLI to pull and fix vulnerabilities: Findings in the dashboard also give you the ability to copy details , making it easy to paste them into an agent conversation.as Markdown or JSONFrontier AI models are making vulnerabilities far easier to find and exploit. Last month, researchers turned two decade-old flaws in PHP core into  with relatively little effort. working remote code execution exploitsAt the same time, agents are writing more of the code teams ship, and each handles security review its own way, or in many cases, not at all.With Vercel Security Review, you can scan every push on every project for vulnerabilities by default, using the security policies you set. Security Review starts with code pushed to GitHub. Next, we're bringing it to deployments from the Vercel CLI and v0, and to repositories that don't deploy on Vercel. We're also working on suggested fixes you can apply directly from the pull request.Vercel Security Review is available today in public beta for Pro and Enterprise teams.To get started, enable Security Review in . You can choose to run Security Review on all projects, or only the ones you choose. To learn more, read the  and the .
